name: ECK-Tunnel end-to-end test: Iran server, Kharej server, user
time_budget: Keep the whole run to about 10 minutes: short measurements, no repeated runs unless a case fails.
role: You are a test engineer. Build and run an end-to-end test of ECK-Tunnel on ONE Ubuntu 22.04 (or newer) Linux machine as root. Simulate three hosts with Linux network namespaces: an Iran server, a Kharej (abroad) server, and an end user. Run every test case below, collect the evidence each one asks for, and write the final report in Persian (fa). Never touch the host's real network config, real /etc/resolv.conf, real apt sources, or any running pengutunnel/eck service; everything happens inside the namespaces and is removed at the end.

inputs.eck_binary: dist/eck-linux-amd64 from the ECK-Tunnel repo (or build: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o eck .)

topology.description: Three namespaces joined by a Linux bridge on the host. The user only ever talks to the Iran server; the Iran server only exposes forwarded ports; the real service runs on the Kharej server.

ns-iran.role: ECK server (Setup Iran). Listens for the tunnel on 8443, exposes user port 9912 (TCP) and 9913 (UDP).

ns-kharej.role: ECK client (Setup Kharej). Dials 10.99.0.1:8443. Runs the real services: HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8080, iperf3 on 127.0.0.1:5201, UDP echo on 127.0.0.1:9000.

setup_commands: ip link add br-eck type bridge && ip link set br-eck up
for n in iran kharej user; do ip netns add ns-$n; ip link add v-$n type veth peer name v-$n-br; ip link set v-$n netns ns-$n; ip link set v-$n-br master br-eck up; ip -n ns-$n link set lo up; done
ip -n ns-iran addr add 10.99.0.1/24 dev v-iran && ip -n ns-iran link set v-iran up
ip -n ns-kharej addr add 10.99.0.2/24 dev v-kharej && ip -n ns-kharej link set v-kharej up
ip -n ns-user addr add 10.99.0.3/24 dev v-user && ip -n ns-user link set v-user up
ip netns exec ns-user ping -c1 -W1 10.99.0.1   # must succeed

iran_network_emulation.purpose: Reproduce what was measured on the real Iran route: added latency, some loss, and a per-connection (per-flow) rate cap — the reason a pool of 8 parallel connections helps.
iran_network_emulation.apply_on: the Kharej side's egress toward Iran (inside ns-kharej, device v-kharej) and the Iran side's egress (ns-iran, v-iran)

profiles.iran: tc qdisc replace dev <dev> root netem delay 60ms 10ms loss 1%
profiles.per_flow_cap: tc qdisc replace dev <dev> root handle 1: netem delay 60ms 10ms loss 0.5% && tc qdisc add dev <dev> parent 1: handle 2: fq maxrate 20mbit   # fq maxrate caps EACH flow at 20 Mbit/s

configs.token: generate once with: head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64  — use the SAME value on both ends
configs.iran_server_toml:
[server]
bind_addr = "0.0.0.0:8443"
transport = "stealth"
token = "<TOKEN>"
ports = ["9912=127.0.0.1:8080", "9914=127.0.0.1:5201", "9913=127.0.0.1:9000"]
accept_udp = true
heartbeat = 10
log_level = "info"
configs.kharej_client_toml:
[client]
remote_addr = "10.99.0.1:8443"
transport = "stealth"
token = "<TOKEN>"
connection_pool = 8
retry_interval = 1
log_level = "info"
kharej_services: ip netns exec ns-kharej python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory /tmp/eck-test/www &
ip netns exec ns-kharej socat -T5 UDP-LISTEN:9000,bind=127.0.0.1,fork EXEC:cat &

test_cases.title: Tunnel comes up
steps: Start Iran, then Kharej.
Wait up to 15 s.
test_cases.check: iran.log and kharej.log show the control channel established; no error lines. `ip netns exec ns-kharej ss -tn dst 10.99.0.1:8443` shows the pooled connections (expect about 8 plus control).
test_cases.pass: tunnel up within 15 s AND at least 8 established connections to 10.99.0.1:8443

test_cases.title: User reaches the real service through the tunnel (HTTP)
steps: ip netns exec ns-user curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://10.99.0.1:9912/

test_cases.title: Data integrity on a 20 MB download
steps: ip netns exec ns-user curl -s http://10.99.0.1:9912/blob.bin | sha256sum
test_cases.pass: hash equals the hash printed when the blob was created

test_cases.title: UDP forwarding
steps: echo eck-udp-probe | ip netns exec ns-user socat -T3 - UDP:10.99.0.1:9913

test_cases.title: Throughput, clean network
steps: ip netns exec ns-user iperf3 -c 10.99.0.1 -p 9914 -t 5 -P 4
ip netns exec ns-user iperf3 -c 10.99.0.1 -p 9914 -t 5 -P 4 -R

test_cases.title: Throughput under the Iran profile and the per-flow cap
steps: Apply profile 'per_flow_cap' on both v-iran and v-kharej.
Repeat T05.
Then set connection_pool = 1 in kharej.toml, restart the Kharej client, repeat T05 again.
test_cases.pass: pool 8 is clearly faster than pool 1 (expect roughly >2x) — this proves the pool spreads traffic across flows the way pengutunnel's 8 connections do

test_cases.title: Wrong token is refused silently
steps: Start a second Kharej client in ns-kharej with a different token.
Watch it for 10 s.
test_cases.pass: it never establishes a tunnel; the Iran side keeps serving the correct client; T02 still passes

test_cases.title: Probe resistance (no fingerprint)
steps: ip netns exec ns-user bash -c 'head -c 512 /dev/urandom | timeout 5 ncat 10.99.0.1 8443 | wc -c'

ip netns exec ns-user bash -c 'printf "GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: x

" | timeout 5 ncat 10.99.0.1 8443 | wc -c'
test_cases.pass: 0 bytes returned in both cases — the tunnel port answers nothing to someone without the token

test_cases.title: Traffic looks random on the wire
steps: ip netns exec ns-iran timeout 10 tcpdump -i v-iran -c 30 -X 'tcp port 8443 and len > 100' while T03 runs.
test_cases.pass: no readable protocol text (no HTTP, no TLS ClientHello 0x16 0x03, no fixed 00 00 length prefix pattern at the start of every record)

test_cases.title: Reconnect after the Kharej side restarts
steps: Kill the Kharej client.
Confirm T02 fails.
Start it again.
Measure seconds until T02 passes again.

test_cases.title: Reconnect after a network cut
steps: ip -n ns-kharej link set v-kharej down; sleep 10; ip -n ns-kharej link set v-kharej up
Measure seconds until T02 passes again.
test_cases.pass: recovers by itself within 45 s with no manual restart

test_cases.title: Many short connections
steps: ip netns exec ns-user bash -c 'ok=0; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /dev/null -m 5 -w "%{http_code}\n" http://10.99.0.1:9912/ | grep -q 200 && ok=$((ok+1)); done; echo $ok'

test_cases.title: Resource use
steps: During T05 record `ps -o rss,pcpu -C eck` in both namespaces.
After 1 minute idle record again.
test_cases.pass: no steady RSS growth while idle (no leak); report the numbers

test_cases.title: Unit and integration test suite
steps: cd <source_tree> && bash scripts/run-tests.sh   # quick mode, a few minutes. Use --full only when asked.
test_cases.pass: go vet clean and every package ok; list any FAIL with its first error lines

test_cases.title: Best DNS and Best apt mirror tools (safe mode)
steps: These change the host's /etc files, so do NOT run them from the menu on the test machine. Their logic is covered by `go test ./internal/systools/` inside T14.

Optionally, on a throwaway VM only: sudo eck → 6 Optimize → Best DNS → Auto, then Restore; → Best apt mirror → Auto (answer y to apt-get update), then Restore. Confirm /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/apt/sources.list are byte-identical to before (sha256sum before/after).
test_cases.pass: suite passes; on the VM, files are identical after Restore

cleanup: for n in iran kharej user; do ip netns del ns-$n; done

sections: خلاصه: چند تست قبول و چند تست رد شد
جدول تست‌ها: شناسه، عنوان، نتیجه (قبول/رد)، عدد اندازه‌گیری‌شده، توضیح کوتاه
مقایسه سرعت: pool 8 در برابر pool 1، شبکه تمیز در برابر پروفایل ایران
خطاها: برای هر تست ردشده، خطوط مهم لاگ iran.log و kharej.log و حدس علت
پیشنهاد: تنظیمات پیشنهادی برای سرور واقعی (transport، connection_pool، MTU)
rules: Report numbers exactly as measured; do not round a failure into a pass.
If a step could not run (missing tool, no root), mark it SKIPPED with the reason — never PASSED.
Remove the token from any log excerpt before putting it in the report.
